subject: science
passage: The kiwi, a flightless bird found only in New Zealand, hunts mostly at night. Unlike other birds, it has its nostrils at the very tip of its long, thin bill, which helps it find food it cannot see. Poking its bill deep into the soil, ______
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: the kiwi sniffs out worms and insects.
choices.B: the soil gives the kiwi the smell of worms and insects.
choices.C: the kiwi's sense of smell finds worms and insects.
choices.D: worms and insects are sniffed out by the kiwi.

explanation.why: The phrase "Poking its bill deep into the soil" describes whoever is doing the poking, so the words right after the comma must name that one: the kiwi. Only one choice places "the kiwi" directly after the introductory phrase.
explanation.A: Correct. "The kiwi" comes right after the introductory phrase, so it is clear the kiwi pokes its bill into the soil.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This choice says the soil poked its bill into the soil, which makes no sense.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This choice says the kiwi's sense of smell poked its bill into the soil; the modifier must describe the bird itself.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This choice places "worms and insects" after the phrase, which says the worms and insects poked their bill into the soil.
